items.text: The loop's watchdog no longer types into a window the user has taken over for their own Claude session; it opens a window of its own instead.
The loop's watchdog waits for a quota's known reset time and retries the moment it clears, instead of nudging every 20 minutes.
When a usage limit pauses the loop, its own window now says so and when it resumes, and the dashboard's blocked bar shows it again.
The rare 4K drag hitch is traced to Windows making the app wait 15-54 ms to take one small picture for the window; parked for an admin trace.
The rare late 4K drag frame is traced to Windows idling inside the one call that moves all the panes; parked on the same admin trace as T2952.
A fold glide no longer stops to wait for a pane that is still hidden behind its strip, so the slowest 120 Hz glide frames are about a third shorter.
Glass panes' backdrop slices are cut from a quarter-size copy of the desk, so a 4K glide's glass step is about a third of what it was.
A one-command performance baseline now measures what Ghoztty costs on Windows, and the first one is committed.
The renderer and GPU audit is done: 17 verified findings are queued, led by a counter that makes panes redraw everything after ~100k frames.
The win32 frontend performance audit is done: 16 verified findings are queued, led by every thread pinning a 16 MB stack.
The memory and leak audit is done: no close path leaks, and 12 verified findings are queued, led by pixel buffers kept at their largest size.
The IPC and agent performance audit is done: 17 verified findings are queued, led by agent and holder threads committing 16 MB stacks each.
The viewer-pane performance audit is done: 24 verified findings are queued, led by the browser processes that outlive the last viewer and hidden viewers that are never suspended.
The shared-core performance audit is done: 16 verified findings are queued, led by NumLock making every mouse move redraw the whole pane.
